title: Hot/Cold Audit Tiering + Query Cost Guardrails for Audit Pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a hot/cold storage tiering strategy for audit events with automated index partitioning and query cost guardrails. Goal: reduce monthly storage cost of audit logs by ~40% (target $/GB), keep recent 7 days in fast hot indices for low-latency lookups, move older events to compacted cold partitions with compressed indexes, and prevent expensive ad-hoc queries from overwhelming the cluster with per-query cost limits and throttles. This work ties to RBAC v2 and admin console controls to let security teams configure retention buckets and emergency hold policies.
acceptance_criteria: Hot index retains most recent 7 days with average query latency <= 200ms for common admin queries (token-level trace, user session, auth events)
Cold partitioning moves events older than 7 days automatically and reduces storage footprint for those events by >= 35% using compression + sparse indexing
Query cost guardrails enforce configurable token/row scan limits per query and reject/queue queries that exceed budget with clear error messages
Operational dashboards surface hot/cold size, rehydration rates, percent of queries hitting cold, and cost saved per retention bucket
Migration plan validated: existing indices older than 30 days moved to coldstore without data loss and with <5% transient error rate during migration window
implementation_plan: Design partitioning schema: daily partitions for hot (7d sliding window), monthly compacted segments for cold, with metadata index referencing shard boundaries
Add ingest-time routing: tag events with retention_bucket and write to hot index; background job moves committed segments older than 7d into cold tier
Implement coldstore format: columnar compressed blobs + minimal metadata index to support bounded audit queries (time ranges, event-type filters)
Build query planner changes: planner chooses hot path when query range intersects hot partitions, otherwise rewrites to cold access with cost estimate
Introduce query cost estimator and enforced budget: estimated rows/scanned_bytes threshold per-request; exceed => return 429 with guidance or enqueue as high-cost job
Exposed admin controls in Console: retention buckets, emergency retention hold (legal/incident), per-team query budgets, and a migration toggle
Add telemetry and dashboards: per-bucket storage, estimated monthly cost, query budget usage, cold rehydrate counts
Create migration tool with dry-run and progress reporting to move historical indices to coldstore
Write e2e tests including load tests, rehydration tests, and failure-mode tests for partial migrations
Coordinate rollout: canary in non-prod, small beta with security team, staged production rollout with monitoring and rollback plan
notes: Trade-offs: more aggressive compaction saves cost but increases rehydration latency for on-demand investigations. Default policy favors 7d hot to keep operator workflows fast.
SLA: Investigations requiring >90d history may be answered via async archival restore (rehydrate job) that has longer SLA but lower storage cost.
Compatibility: Ensure RBAC v2 respects per-team retention settings; audit records tied to customer/org must always respect their policy and legal holds.
We should consider leveraging existing coldstore (blob-backed) used by metrics infra to avoid duplicate infra work; requires API compatibility checks.
Cost model: initial projection shows 38% reduction on current bucket if cold compression ratio meets 4x. We will instrument to validate.

Open question: whether to allow ad-hoc SQL-style cross-month queries to transparently span hot+cold or require user to opt-in to long-running queries. Proposal: default reject with suggested async job endpoint.
Security review notes: coldstore encryption must use KMS keys scoped to customer org where required; audit of access to rehydration APIs must be logged and visible in console.
